29776:
The cut along AB contains the principal axis, so each half keeps both refracting surfaces with focal length and power unchanged at 4\text{ D}.
The cut along CD separates the two curved surfaces into plano-convex halves of double focal length, so each has power P / 2 = 2\text{ D}.
Each quadrant undergoes both cuts, hence its power is 2\text{ D} → (D)
29777:
At terminal velocity the acceleration is zero, so M g = F_B + F_v.
The buoyant force is F_B = V \rho_g g with \rho_g = \rho_{ball} / 2, giving F_B = M g / 2.
Hence F_v = M g - M g / 2 = M g / 2 → (B)
29778:
With \rho = m / (\pi r^2 l), the fractional error is \frac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} = \frac{\Delta m}{m} + 2 \frac{\Delta r}{r} + \frac{\Delta l}{l}.
Substituting gives 0.003 / 0.60 + 2 (0.01 / 0.50) + 0.05 / 10.00 = 0.005 + 0.040 + 0.005 = 0.050.
The maximum percentage error is 0.050 \times 100 = 5\% → (B)
29779:
At resonance X_L = X_C, so the impedance is Z = R and I_0 = E_0 / R.
Doubling the resistance to 2R gives I_0' = E_0 / (2R) = I_0 / 2 → (B)
29780:
Point A is axial at distance r, so V_A = kP / r^2 = V_0 and E_A = 2kP / r^3 = E_0 with P along x.
Point B is equatorial at distance 2r, where the potential is always zero, so V_B = 0.
The field there is kP / (2r)^3 = kP / (8r^3) = E_0 / 16 → (C)
29781:
Capacitance is C = q / V = q^2 / W with work W = M L^2 T^{-2}.
So the dimensions are C^2 / (M L^2 T^{-2}) = C^2 M^{-1} L^{-2} T^2 → (D)
29782:
Circular motion in the field gives m v = e B r, i.e. m v r = e B r^2.
Bohr quantization m v r = n h / (2\pi) then gives r = \sqrt{n h / (2\pi e B)}.
The first excited state has n = 2, so r = \sqrt{h / (\pi e B)} → (D)
29783:
For an ideal gas \gamma = 1 + 2 / f where f counts the degrees of freedom.
Rigid diatomic molecules have f = 5 giving \gamma_1 = 1.40, while extra vibrational modes raise f to 7 giving \gamma_2 = 1 + 2 / 7 \approx 1.29.
Hence \gamma_2 < \gamma_1 → (D)
29784:
The motional emf is \varepsilon = B l v with l the side length inside the field.
Since B, l and v stay constant while the loop exits, \varepsilon stays constant.
The flat horizontal graph is labelled (4) → (D)
29785:
The first beam gives h c / \lambda = \phi + K_{max} = 1 + 2 = 3\text{ eV}.
Halving the wavelength doubles the photon energy to 6\text{ eV}.
The new maximum kinetic energy is K_{max}' = 6 - 1 = 5\text{ eV} → (C)
29786:
On the planet g' = G (4M) / (2R)^2 = G M / R^2 = g, so T = 2\pi\sqrt{l / g} is unchanged and assertion (A) is true.
The pendulum mass is indeed unchanged, so reason (R) is also true.
But the period never depends on the bob mass, so (R) does not explain (A) → (A)
29787:
Torque is \vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} with \vec{r} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k} and \vec{F} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}.
The components are \tau_x = (1)(2) - (1)(1) = 1, \tau_y = (1)(2) - (1)(2) = 0 and \tau_z = (1)(1) - (1)(2) = -1.
So \vec{\tau} = \hat{i} - \hat{k} → (C)
29788:
The upper AND gate outputs A \cdot \bar{B} and the lower AND gate outputs \bar{A} \cdot B.
The table needs output 1 exactly for inputs (0, 0) and (1, 1), which is the XNOR of these two signals.
A NOR gate at G gives Y = \overline{(A \cdot \bar{B}) + (\bar{A} \cdot B)}, matching the table → (A)
29789:
Work is W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{S} = (2)(1) + (b)(-2) + (1)(-1) = 1 - 2b.
Zero work gives 1 - 2b = 0, so b = 1 / 2 → (B)
29790:
Fringe width \beta = \lambda D / d is directly proportional to wavelength, so reason (R) is true.
Since \lambda_{red} > \lambda_{blue}, red fringes are spaced wider apart, so assertion (A) is false → (B)
29791:
Initial kinetic energy is (1 / 2) (0.1) (20)^2 = 20\text{ J}.
At the top only v_x = 20 \cos 60^\circ = 10\text{ m/s} remains, giving (1 / 2) (0.1) (10)^2 = 5\text{ J}.
The decrease is 20 - 5 = 15\text{ J} → (B)
29792:
Reflection at the air-film boundary suffers a \pi phase shift since the film is denser, while the film-glass boundary suffers none since glass is rarer.
Cancelling the reflection then needs path difference 2\mu t = \lambda, so t_{min} = \lambda / (2\mu).
With \lambda = 550\text{ nm} and \mu = 2.0, t_{min} = 550 / 4 = 137.5\text{ nm} → (C)
29793:
Continuity of flow gives A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2, i.e. \pi r_1^2 v_1 = \pi r_2^2 v_2.
With r_1 = 2\text{ cm}, r_2 = 1\text{ cm} and v_1 = 2\text{ m/s}, v_2 = (4)(2) / 1 = 8\text{ m/s} → (D)
29794:
Extensive variables scale with system size: internal energy, volume and mass are extensive, so statement (A) is correct.
Intensive variables do not: pressure, temperature and density are intensive, so statement (B) is correct.
Statements (C) and (D) each misclassify one variable, hence (A) and (B) only → (C)
29795:
At A the energy is K_A = (1 / 2) (0.1) (10)^2 = 5\text{ J} with radius R = 2\text{ m}.
Point B sits R(1 - \cos 30^\circ) = 2 - \sqrt{3} above A, so K_B = 5 - (0.1)(10)(2 - \sqrt{3}) = 3 + \sqrt{3}.
Point C sits R(1 + \sin 30^\circ) = 3\text{ m} above A, so K_C = 5 - 3 = 2 and K_B / K_C = (3 + \sqrt{3}) / 2 → (C)
29796:
Undeflected motion needs electric and magnetic forces to balance, so v = E / B.
With E switched off, the circular radius r = m v / (q B) gives B = m v / (q r), so E = m v^2 / (q r).
Substituting gives E = (1.6 \times 10^{-27}) (2 \times 10^5)^2 / ((1.6 \times 10^{-19})(0.02)) = 2 \times 10^4\text{ N/C}, so x = 2 → (2)
29797:
Point P lies 4\text{ cm} from wire Y and 10\text{ cm} from wire X on the same line, and the opposite currents make the two fields oppose.
The resultant is B_P = (\mu_0 / (2\pi)) (I_Y / d_Y - I_X / d_X).
With \mu_0 / (2\pi) = 2 \times 10^{-7}, B_P = (2 \times 10^{-7})(4 / 0.04 - 5 / 0.10) = 1 \times 10^{-5}\text{ T}, so x = 1 → (1)
29798:
The displacement current through the full plate area equals the conduction current of 6\text{ A}.
The uniform field gives I_d = 6 (A_0 / A) = 6 (3.2 / 16) = 1.2\text{ A} through area A_0.
In milliamperes this is 1200 → (1200)
29799:
The liquid force is F = \int_0^l ((2M / l) \omega^2 x) dx = M l \omega^2.
With tube length l = 1\text{ m}, F = M \omega^2 gives \omega = \sqrt{F / M}.
Matching \sqrt{F / (\alpha M)} gives \alpha = 1 → (1)
29800:
In DC steady state the capacitor branch is open, so the entire right section draws no current.
On the left, 3\Omega \parallel 6\Omega = 2\Omega in series with 2\Omega gives 4\Omega, which in parallel with the 4\Omega branch yields R_{eq} = 2\Omega.
Net current I = 2 / 2 = 1\text{ A} → (1)
29802:
Ionisation enthalpy rises across the period with a dip between nitrogen and oxygen
Values order as boron 801 < carbon 1086 < oxygen 1314 < nitrogen 1402 in \text{kJ mol}^{-1}
Nitrogen exceeds oxygen because its half-filled 2p^{3} shell resists electron loss
Hence the order is \text{B} < \text{C} < \text{O} < \text{N} → (A)
29803:
Linkage isomerism needs an ambidentate ligand binding through either donor atom
Nitrite binds as nitro (\text{-NO}_2) or nitrito (\text{-ONO})
Only [\text{Co(NH}_3)_5(\text{NO}_2)]\text{Cl}_2 among the choices carries such a ligand → (A)
29804:
Forward barrier runs from the reactant level to the activated-complex peak
Peak height above reactant = E_1 + E_2 from the figure
Product level lies above reactant level, so the step is endothermic and product is less stable
Forward activation energy E_1 + E_2 with less stable product → (C)
29805:
Sunlight bromination replaces the hydrogen whose radical is most stable
Tertiary radicals outrank secondary and primary ones
The side-chain tertiary C-H cleaves to the most stable acyclic 3^{\circ} radical while ring positions are less reactive
Bromine therefore installs at that side-chain carbon, the structure labelled (4) → (D)
29807:
Amide \text{RCONH}_2 reduces to amine with \text{LiAlH}_4, reagent (III)
Nitrobenzene reduces with Sn / HCl, reagent (IV), and nitrile \text{RCN} with \text{H}_2 / \text{Ni}, reagent (II)
N-substituted phthalimide hydrolyses with aqueous NaOH, reagent (I)
Pairing (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(II), (D)-(I) → (D)
29808:
Grignard formation followed by hydrolysis replaces \text{-Br} by \text{-H} on the same skeleton
Every structural isomer of bromo-2-methylbutane therefore gives 2-methylbutane
Bromine can sit on four distinct carbons of the 2-methylbutane skeleton
Four qualifying RBr isomers → (A)
29809:
From dG = V dP - S dT, (\frac{\partial G}{\partial T})_p = -S, entry (II)
Definitions give (\frac{\partial H}{\partial T})_p = C_p, entry (I), and (\frac{\partial G}{\partial P})_T = V, entry (IV)
Likewise (\frac{\partial U}{\partial T})_v = C_v, entry (III)
The pairing (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(III) → (B)
29810:
CFSE grows with oxidation state, so cobalt(III) outranks cobalt(II)
Octahedral splitting exceeds tetrahedral, placing [\text{Co(NH}_3)_4]^{2+} lowest
Ligand field en > \text{NH}_3 puts [\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+} at the top
Order [\text{Co(NH}_3)_4]^{2+} < [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{2+} < [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+} < [\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+} → (B)
29813:
Carbocation stability is set by electron donation into the empty p orbital
Para-methoxy donates strongly by +M resonance, outweighing methyl hyperconjugation or unsubstituted phenyl
Meta-methoxy cannot conjugate, so p-methoxybenzyl cation wins → (A)
29814:
Extreme-left elements are alkali and alkaline-earth metals forming basic oxides, so statement (I) is false
Extreme-right reactive nonmetals form acidic oxides that yield acids with water, so statement (II) is true
False-true combination → (A)
29815:
Orbitals 2p_x and 2p_y share the same energy without external field, so statement (II) is true
A 2p_x \rightarrow 2p_y jump has \Delta E = 0 and emits no photon, so statement (I) is false
False-true combination → (D)
29816:
Lassaigne fusion detects nitrogen, sulphur, halogens and phosphorus, so statement (I) is true
Fusion uses molten sodium, not magnesium, so statement (II) is false
True-false combination → (C)
29817:
Homoleptic means one ligand type, ruling out [\text{Fe(CN)}_5\text{NO}]^{2-}
Weak-field \text{F}^{-} and \text{H}_2\text{O} keep (B) and (E) high spin
Strong-field \text{CN}^{-} and \text{NH}_3 on d^{6} give low-spin [\text{Fe(CN)}_6]^{4-} (C) and [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+} (D)
Pair (C) and (D) only → (C)
29819:
Corrosion is electrochemical with metal oxidising at the anode, so statement (I) is true
\text{H}^{+} drives the cathodic step, so attack runs faster in acid than in alkali and statement (II) is false
True-false combination → (D)
29820:
Secondary hydrogens sit only on \text{-CH}_2\text{-} carbons
The isomer 2,2,3,3-tetramethylpentane is \text{CH}_3\text{C(CH}_3)_2\text{C(CH}_3)_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3 with a single \text{CH}_2 group
That group carries exactly two secondary hydrogens while every other choice has more → (C)
29821:
Four moles of \text{H}_2 per mole mean four \pi bonds consumed
Four \pi bonds hold 2 \times 4 = 8 \pi electrons
Single monobromo product confirms the symmetric dialkyne layout → (8)
29822:
Niobium (Z = 41) is [\text{Kr}] 4d^{4} 5s^{1}, so x = 4
Ruthenium (Z = 44) is [\text{Kr}] 4d^{7} 5s^{1}, so y = 7
Sum x + y = 4 + 7 = 11 → (11)
29823:
The red complex is [\text{Ni(dmg)}_2] with two dimethylglyoximate ligands
Each bound ligand is \text{C}_4\text{H}_7\text{N}_2\text{O}_2 after losing one oxime proton
Total hydrogen = 2 \times 7 = 14 → (14)
29824:
Target formation is 2 \text{C} + 3 \text{H}_2 \rightarrow \text{C}_2\text{H}_6
Combining 2 \times (2) + 3 \times (3) - (1) by Hess law
\Delta H_f^{\circ} = 2(-393.5) + 3(-286) - (-1550) = -787 - 858 + 1550 = -95 \text{ kJ mol}^{-1}
Magnitude 95 → (95)
29826:
On a set with n = 6 elements a reflexive relation must contain all 6 diagonal pairs.
Symmetry forces off-diagonal pairs to enter with their mirrors, so group them into C(6, 2) = 15 unordered pairs.
Each unordered pair is independently kept or dropped, giving 2^{15} reflexive symmetric relations.
Forbidding the ordered pair (1, 2) forces the unordered pair {1, 2} to be dropped.
The remaining 14 unordered pairs stay free, giving 2^{14} relations.
This matches option A → (A)
29827:
For the equation x^2 - x + 1 = 0 the discriminant is \Delta = 1 - 4 = -3, so the roots are non-real conjugates.
By the quadratic formula \alpha, \beta = \frac{1 \pm i \sqrt{3}}{2}, which have modulus 1.
In polar form \alpha = e^{\frac{i \pi}{3}} and \beta = e^{\frac{-i \pi}{3}}, since \cos \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{1}{2} and \sin \frac{\pi}{3} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.
By De Moivre theorem \alpha^{2024} + \beta^{2024} = e^{\frac{2024 i \pi}{3}} + e^{\frac{-2024 i \pi}{3}} = 2 \cos \frac{2024 \pi}{3}.
Since 2024 = 6 \times 337 + 2, the angle reduces as \frac{2024 \pi}{3} = 674 \pi + \frac{2 \pi}{3}.
Hence the sum equals 2 \cos \frac{2 \pi}{3} = 2 \times \frac{-1}{2} = -1.
This matches option A → (A)
29828:
For a 3 \times 3 system to have infinitely many solutions the third equation must repeat the second, since the first two are independent.
Comparing x + 2y + \lambda z = \mu with x + 2y + 3z = 10 gives \lambda = 3 and \mu = 10.
With these values the third equation is identical to the second, leaving two independent equations in three unknowns.
Two planes meeting in a line give infinitely many solutions, so the condition is consistent.
Adding gives \lambda + \mu = 3 + 10 = 13.
This matches option A → (A)
29830:
Write y = \frac{x^2 - 1}{x^2 + 1} and solve for x^2 in terms of y.
Cross-multiplying gives yx^2 + y = x^2 - 1, hence x^2 (1 - y) = 1 + y.
Real x needs x^2 \ge 0, so \frac{1 + y}{1 - y} \ge 0 with y \neq 1.
The quotient stays non-negative exactly for -1 \le y < 1.
At y = -1 we get x = 0, while y = 1 would divide by zero and stays excluded.
Hence the range is [-1, 1), which matches option A → (A)
29831:
Recall the Maclaurin series \sin x = x - \frac{x^3}{6} + \frac{x^5}{120} - \cdots.
Subtracting the first two terms leaves \sin x - x + \frac{x^3}{6} = \frac{x^5}{120} - \cdots.
Dividing by x^5 gives \frac{1}{120} plus terms that still contain positive powers of x.
By the limit theorem each surviving term tends to 0 as x \to 0.
Hence the limit equals \frac{1}{120}.
This matches option A → (A)
29833:
Denote the integral by I and recall the King property \int_0^a f(x) dx = \int_0^a f(a - x) dx.
With a = \frac{\pi}{2} the substitution x \to \frac{\pi}{2} - x swaps \sin x and \cos x.
Hence I = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} \frac{\sqrt{\cos x}}{\sqrt{\cos x} + \sqrt{\sin x}} dx.
Adding the two forms gives 2I = \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{2}} 1 dx = \frac{\pi}{2}.
Dividing yields I = \frac{\pi}{4}.
This matches option A → (A)
29834:
Find the meeting points by writing x = \frac{y^2}{4} from the parabola and x = \frac{y + 4}{2} from the line.
Equating gives \frac{y^2}{4} = \frac{y + 4}{2}, hence y^2 - 2y - 8 = 0.
Factoring yields (y - 4)(y + 2) = 0, so the curves meet at y = -2 and y = 4.
Slicing horizontally makes the area A = \int_{-2}^{4} (\frac{y + 4}{2} - \frac{y^2}{4}) dy.
An antiderivative is \frac{y^2}{4} + 2y - \frac{y^3}{12}, which evaluates to 9 across the limits.
This matches option A → (A)
29835:
Recall that \cos \theta = \frac{\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b}}{|\vec{a}| |\vec{b}|} for vectors \vec{a} and \vec{b}.
The dot product is \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} = 2 \times 1 + 2 \times (-2) + (-1) \times 2 = -4.
The moduli are |\vec{a}| = \sqrt{4 + 4 + 1} = 3 and |\vec{b}| = \sqrt{1 + 4 + 4} = 3.
Dividing gives \cos \theta = \frac{-4}{3 \times 3} = \frac{-4}{9}.
This matches option A → (A)
29837:
Model each roll as a Bernoulli trial with success probability p = \frac{1}{6} for a six.
The total X over n = 2 independent trials is Binomial with variance np(1 - p).
Substituting gives \text{Var}(X) = 2 \times \frac{1}{6} \times \frac{5}{6}.
Multiplying out yields \frac{10}{36} = \frac{5}{18}.
This matches option A → (A)
29838:
Recall the complementary identity \cos^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} x = \frac{\pi}{2} for x in [-1, 1].
Apply it to both x and y, then add the two identities.
This gives (\cos^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} y) + (\sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} y) = \pi.
Insert the hypothesis \sin^{-1} x + \sin^{-1} y = \frac{2\pi}{3}.
Hence \cos^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} y = \pi - \frac{2\pi}{3} = \frac{\pi}{3}.
This matches option A → (A)
29839:
Divide 9x^2 - 16y^2 = 144 by 144 to reach standard form \frac{x^2}{16} - \frac{y^2}{9} = 1.
Read off a^2 = 16 and b^2 = 9 for this x-transverse hyperbola.
Recall the eccentricity formula e = \sqrt{1 + \frac{b^2}{a^2}}.
Substituting gives e = \sqrt{1 + \frac{9}{16}} = \sqrt{\frac{25}{16}}.
Taking the root yields e = \frac{5}{4}.
This matches option A → (A)
29840:
For a 3 \times 3 matrix recall \det(\operatorname{adj}(A)) = (\det A)^{3 - 1}.
With \det(A) = 3 this gives \det(\operatorname{adj}(A)) = 3^2 = 9.
Scalar multiplication in 3 dimensions scales the determinant as \det(2M) = 2^3 \det(M).
Applying this with M = \operatorname{adj}(A) gives 8 \times 9 = 72.
This matches option A → (A)
29841:
Differentiate to get f'(x) = 6x^2 - 18x + 12 = 6(x - 1)(x - 2).
The critical points inside [0, 3] are therefore x = 1 and x = 2.
Evaluate f at the endpoints and at the critical points for comparison.
The values are f(0) = 5 and f(1) = 10.
Also f(2) = 9 and f(3) = 14.
The smallest of these is 5, attained at x = 0.
This matches option A → (A)
29842:
A line parallel to 2x + y = 3 has the form 2x + y = k with slope -2.
Write it as y = -2x + k and recall the tangency condition c^2 = a^2 m^2 + b^2.
Here m = -2 with a^2 = 25 and b^2 = 16 from the ellipse.
Substituting gives k^2 = 25 \times 4 + 16 = 116.
Hence k = \pm \sqrt{116}.
The tangents are 2x + y = \pm \sqrt{116}, which matches option A → (A)
29844:
Substitute u = 1 - x so that x = 1 - u with dx = -du and matching limits.
The integral becomes \int_0^1 (1 - u) u^9 du.
Expanding gives \int_0^1 (u^9 - u^{10}) du.
Integrating termwise yields \frac{1}{10} - \frac{1}{11}.
Combining gives \frac{11 - 10}{110} = \frac{1}{110}.
This matches option A → (A)
29845:
Split each term by partial fractions as \frac{1}{(2k - 1)(2k + 1)} = \frac{1}{2} (\frac{1}{2k - 1} - \frac{1}{2k + 1}).
The partial sums therefore telescope across consecutive values of k.
Summing to N gives S_N = \frac{1}{2} (1 - \frac{1}{2N + 1}).
Letting N \to \infty sends the trailing fraction to 0.
The infinite sum is hence \frac{1}{2}.
This matches option A → (A)
29846:
Find an antiderivative via the power rule as F(x) = \frac{x^4}{4} - x^3 + x^2.
Evaluate at the upper limit to get F(2) = 4 - 8 + 4 = 0.
At the lower limit F(0) = 0.
Subtracting gives k = F(2) - F(0) = 0.
Multiplying by 12 keeps 12k = 12 \times 0 = 0.
Hence the required value is (0)
29847:
Recall the m-th term from partial sums as T_m = S_m - S_{m - 1}.
Insert S_n = 3n^2 + 5n to get T_m = (3m^2 + 5m) - (3(m - 1)^2 + 5(m - 1)).
Expanding gives T_m = 6m + 2.
Set this equal to 164, so 6m + 2 = 164.
Solving yields 6m = 162 and hence m = 27.
Hence the required value is (27)
29850:
Let the two unknown observations be a and b with n = 7 and mean 8.
The total is 7 \times 8 = 56 while 2 + 4 + 10 + 12 + 14 = 42.
Hence a + b = 56 - 42 = 14.
Variance 16 gives \frac{1}{7} \sum x_i^2 - 64 = 16, so \sum x_i^2 = 560.
The five known squares sum to 4 + 16 + 100 + 144 + 196 = 460, leaving a^2 + b^2 = 100.
Since (a + b)^2 = a^2 + b^2 + 2ab, substitution gives 196 = 100 + 2ab.
Thus ab = 48, so the required product is (48)
29829:
In (1 - x + 2 x^2)^5 choose a factors of (-x) and b factors of (2 x^2) with a + 2 b = 7 and a + b \le 5.
Only the pairs (a, b) = (3, 2) and (1, 3) satisfy both conditions.
The first gives \frac{5!}{3! 2!} (-1)^3 2^2 = 10 \times (-4) = -40.
The second gives \frac{5!}{1! 3! 1!} (-1) 2^3 = 20 \times (-8) = -160.
Total coefficient = -40 - 160 = -200 matches none of 30, -30, -40, 40, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
29832:
Rewriting gives \frac{dy}{dx} - \frac{2}{x} y = \frac{1}{x^2}, a linear equation with integrating factor x^{-2}.
Multiplying through yields \frac{d}{dx} (y x^{-2}) = x^{-4}.
Integrating gives y x^{-2} = -\frac{1}{3 x^3} + C.
Passing through (1, 1) gives 1 = -\frac{1}{3} + C, so C = \frac{4}{3}.
Hence y = \frac{4 x^3 - 1}{3 x}, while option A with 4 x^2 fails the ODE, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
29836:
The line through (1, 2, 3) with direction ratios (2, 3, 6) is (1 + 2 t, 2 + 3 t, 3 + 6 t).
That direction has length \sqrt{4 + 9 + 36} = 7.
On 2 x - y + 2 z = 9 this gives 2 + 4 t - 2 - 3 t + 6 + 12 t = 9, so 6 + 13 t = 9 and t = \frac{3}{13}.
Distance along the line is |t| \times 7 = \frac{3}{13} \times 7 = \frac{21}{13}.
None of \frac{7}{3}, 7, 1, 2 matches, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
29843:
Four-digit numbers from 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 without repetition total 5 \times 5 \times 4 \times 3 = 300.
Above 4321, thousands digit 5 leaves P(5, 3) = 60 numbers.
With thousands digit 4 only hundreds digit 5 exceeds 3, giving 1 \times P(4, 2) = 12 numbers.
With prefix 435 only tens digit 3 is available above 2, giving 1 \times 3 = 3 numbers.
With prefix 4353 only units digit 2 is available above 1, giving 1 number.
Total 60 + 12 + 3 + 1 = 76 matches none of 180, 194, 198, 186, so the question carries full marks for all attempted → (Bonus)
29848:
Here |\vec{a}|^2 = 4 + 1 + 4 = 9 and the data gives \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = |\vec{c}|.
Expanding |\vec{c} - \vec{a}|^2 = |\vec{c}|^2 - 2 |\vec{c}| + 9 = 8 yields (|\vec{c}| - 1)^2 = 0, so |\vec{c}| = 1.
The cross product \vec{a} \times \vec{b} = 2 \hat{i} - 2 \hat{j} + \hat{k} has magnitude \sqrt{4 + 4 + 1} = 3.
Hence |(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \times \vec{c}| = 3 \times 1 \times \sin 30° = \frac{3}{2}.
